glossaryPage.label: Glossary
glossaryPage.title: 7aychain Terminology
glossaryPage.description: Definitions of key terms, pallets, and concepts in the 7aychain Proof of Presence protocol — from witness circles to ZK circuits.

autonomousDetection.definition: An on-chain pallet that automatically flags anomalous patterns in presence attestations. Detects coordinated Sybil behavior, spoofed timing, and statistical outliers without requiring manual reports.

boomerangProof.definition: A cryptographic proof that an actor returned to a previously attested location. Proves consistent presence patterns over time without revealing the location itself — enabling reputation without surveillance.

circuitRegistry.definition: The on-chain registry of ZK circuits available for proof generation and verification. Manages circuit versions, proof mode migration (stub to full SNARK), and verifier configurations.

commitRevealScheme.definition: A two-phase anti-tampering protocol: actors first commit a hash of their presence data (hiding it), then reveal the actual data in a later phase. Prevents front-running and ensures fair ordering.

deviceScanner.definition: A pallet for registering devices that participate in presence attestation. Manages device identity, attestation capability, and revocation — ensuring only authorized hardware contributes to verification.

disputeResolution.definition: The on-chain process for challenging presence attestations. Disputants submit cryptographic evidence, validators vote, and the protocol enforces outcomes — including slashing for dishonest attestors.

epoch.definition: A fixed time window during which presence declarations, attestations, and finalizations occur. Epochs structure the protocol lifecycle, determine validator rotation, and isolate verification rounds.

groth16.definition: A zero-knowledge proof system used by 7aychain for succinct, non-interactive presence proofs. Delivers constant-size proofs with fast on-chain verification — critical for scalable privacy.

laudNetworksCli.definition: A Python-based terminal user interface (TUI) for interacting with all 16 7aychain pallets. Supports presence declaration, validator management, ZK proofs, governance, vaults, and more.

lifecycle.definition: The six-state machine governing a presence declaration: Declare, Commit, Reveal, Attest, Triangulate, and Finalize. Each transition is enforced by the protocol with epoch-bound constraints.

multilateration.definition: A positioning technique that estimates physical location from network latency measurements taken at multiple validator reference points. The core triangulation algorithm powering witness circles.

octopusGroups.definition: Organizational units that group validators and actors for coordinated presence operations. Groups can define shared governance rules and collective attestation thresholds.

positionBoundToken.definition: A cryptographic token minted when presence is finalized. PBTs bind attestation claims to specific positions and epochs, serving as verifiable proof-of-presence credentials — without revealing exact locations.

presenceLifecycle.definition: The six-phase protocol flow: Declare (announce intent), Commit (submit presence hash), Reveal (disclose data), Attest (validators measure), Triangulate (compute position), Finalize (quorum seal).

proofOfPresence.definition: 7aychain's consensus mechanism. Validators form witness circles and triangulate physical presence through network latency measurement — no GPS, no biometrics, no external hardware. Sybil-resistant by design.

quorumConsensus.definition: The validator agreement threshold required to finalize a presence attestation. A declaration is only finalized when a sufficient percentage of the witness circle converges on a position estimate.

semanticLinks.definition: On-chain relationships between entities (actors, locations, organizations) forming a trust graph. Enable contextual verification and reputation scoring based on verified presence history.

shamirSecretSharing.definition: A cryptographic scheme used in 7aychain's vault system to split sensitive data across multiple parties. No single party holds enough to reconstruct the secret — enabling secure recovery without central custody.

snark.definition: Succinct Non-interactive Argument of Knowledge. A zero-knowledge proof type used by 7aychain for compact, efficiently verifiable presence proofs. The protocol migrates from stub verifiers to full SNARK circuits.

storageLayer.definition: A pallet providing on-chain and off-chain data storage for presence proofs, attestation records, and protocol state. Supports pinning, retrieval, and data availability guarantees.

triangulation.definition: The process by which validators estimate physical position using network latency measurements from multiple reference points. Combines multilateration with centroid algorithms for high-confidence position estimation.

validator.definition: A node operator who stakes $7AY to participate in consensus, presence attestation, and witness circle triangulation. Earns rewards for honest behavior; faces slashing for dishonesty.

vault.definition: A secure on-chain storage system using Shamir secret sharing for distributed key management. Enables data recovery and controlled sharing between authorized parties — without central custody.

witnessCircle.definition: A pseudorandomly selected subset of validators assigned to attest a presence declaration. Circle members independently measure latency and collectively triangulate the actor's physical position.

zkCircuit.definition: A zero-knowledge computation circuit that generates proofs verifying presence without revealing exact location data. 7aychain uses Groth16 circuits with an on-chain registry and a migration path from stub to full SNARK verification.

whyPresencePage.label: Why Presence
whyPresencePage.title: The Internet Lost the Human Signal
whyPresencePage.description: When bots replicate everything humans do online, the only unforgeable proof left is physical presence.

presenceInfrastructure.paragraph1: At the heart of 7aychain is a simple principle: your internet connection can prove where you are. Validators across the network measure connection timing from multiple points, confirming physical location without GPS, cameras, or specialized hardware.
presenceInfrastructure.paragraph2: Most systems verify identity through behavior, accounts, or credentials. At scale, all can be faked. 7aychain takes a fundamentally different approach: it uses the laws of physics.

physicsArgument.label: The Physics Argument
physicsArgument.title: Sybil resistance through physical reality
physicsArgument.subtitle: Instead of trusting profiles, credentials, or biometrics, 7aychain exploits a fundamental constraint: you can only be in one place at a time.

0.title: Physics, Not Scans
0.description: Internet signals obey the speed of light. 7aychain uses this constraint to confirm where you are. No iris scans. No selfies. No fingerprints.

1.title: One Place at a Time
1.description: Create a million accounts — you can still only physically occupy one location. That constraint makes Sybil attacks nearly impossible.

2.title: No Lasting Footprint
2.description: Each verification is ephemeral. No persistent profile, no behavioral tracking, no stored data. Prove you were here, then it's done.

coreInsight.label: Core Insight
coreInsight.title: In a world of perfect simulation, physical reality is the scarce resource
coreInsight.description: AI generates convincing text, behavior, and interaction at scale. But physical presence — being at a specific location at a specific time, measurable through network physics — remains constrained by natural law.

0.response: AI fakes text, transactions, and social activity. It cannot fake being somewhere. Physical presence is bound by the laws of physics.

1.response: New wallets cost nothing. Being in two places at once is impossible. 7aychain converts a digital problem into a physical constraint.

2.response: Iris scans and facial recognition create permanent databases of your body. 7aychain measures internet timing — it never sees your face or knows your name.

3.response: Coordinated groups fabricate social proof. Physical presence is independently verified by the network — no trust assumptions required.

validatorsPage.description: Validators power 7aychain. They form witness circles, measure network latency, triangulate physical presence, and keep the protocol honest.

roleOverview.label: Role Overview
roleOverview.title: What validators do
roleOverview.paragraph1: On 7aychain, validators do more than produce blocks. They actively verify that people are where they claim to be — forming witness circles that independently confirm each person's location through network latency measurement.
roleOverview.paragraph2: Each validator in a witness circle measures round-trip latency to the declaring actor and to other validators. These measurements feed into multilateration algorithms that triangulate physical position — without GPS or external hardware.
roleOverview.paragraph3: When enough validators agree on a position, the presence is confirmed and permanently sealed on-chain. Honest validators earn rewards. Dishonest ones get slashed.
roleOverview.paragraph4: The validator set rotates per epoch, preventing any single group from colluding to falsify presence attestations over time.

witnessCircles.label: Protocol
witnessCircles.title: Witness circle participation
witnessCircles.paragraph1: When an actor declares presence, the protocol selects a subset of active validators to form a
witnessCircles.paragraph1cont: . Selection is pseudorandom, weighted by stake and constrained by network topology.
witnessCircles.paragraph2: Each validator in the circle independently measures round-trip latency to the declaring actor and to other circle members. These measurements are submitted as signed attestations during the commit phase.
witnessCircles.paragraph3: During the reveal phase, latency measurements feed into multilateration — a triangulation algorithm that estimates physical position from network timing data across multiple reference points.
witnessCircles.paragraph4: If the position estimate from a quorum of validators converges within an acceptable threshold, the presence is finalized. Outlier measurements trigger dispute resolution, and validators providing false attestations face slashing.

0.title: 7aychain v0.8.26 released
0.summary: Latest stable release with the complete Proof of Presence protocol stack.
0.content: Released 7aychain v0.8.26 — the latest stable version of the Layer 1 blockchain. Includes the complete protocol stack: presence lifecycle with commit-reveal, witness-circle triangulation, ZK proof verification, validator staking/slashing, governance, vaults, semantic linking, dispute resolution, device scanning, and autonomous detection. Multi-node devnet running with 6 validators.

1.title: Governance and vault system shipped
1.summary: On-chain governance with proposals/voting and secure vault infrastructure.
1.content: Shipped on-chain governance with proposals, voting, and delegation. Implemented the vault system with create, share, recover, register-file, request-unlock, and authorize-unlock operations. Added semantic linking for trust graphs between on-chain entities.

2.title: ZK circuits and triangulation integrated
2.summary: Zero-knowledge proofs and multilateration algorithms now live on devnet.
2.content: Integrated ZK proof generation and on-chain verification for privacy-preserving presence attestation. Implemented multilateration and centroid triangulation algorithms that determine position from network latency measurements without GPS. Added position-bound tokens (PBTs) for cryptographic position claims.

3.title: Validator system and dispute resolution
3.summary: Complete validator lifecycle: registration, staking, slashing, and disputes.
3.content: Implemented the complete validator system: registration, activation, deactivation, withdrawal, staking, and slashing. Added dispute resolution with evidence submission, voting, and on-chain enforcement. Validators form witness circles and participate in quorum-based presence finalization.

4.title: Multi-node devnet and CLI launched
4.summary: Hybrid devnet with 6 validators and Laud Networks CLI for full protocol interaction.
4.content: Launched multi-node hybrid devnet with Alice running natively and remaining validators (Bob, Charlie, Dave, Eve, Ferdie) in Docker. Released the Laud Networks CLI with interactive commands for all protocol modules: presence, epoch, validator, triangulation, ZK, governance, vault, semantic, and more.

5.title: Presence and epoch core shipped
5.summary: Foundational presence lifecycle and epoch management — the protocol backbone.
5.content: Built the core presence state machine (Declared, Attested, Triangulated, Finalized) with epoch-bound lifecycle. Implemented the 5-state epoch model with dynamic state derivation from block timestamps. Established actor/epoch isolation and authority-controlled mutations.

6.title: Problem validation complete
6.summary: Validated core problem with early teams across events, communities, and logistics.
6.content: Validated core problem with early teams. Conducted structured interviews and research across event organizers, community builders, and logistics operators. Confirmed that presence verification is a high-pain, low-solution problem space.

mission.label: What We're Building
mission.title: Our Mission
mission.paragraph1: 7ayLabs builds 7aychain, a new kind of Layer 1 blockchain. Instead of scanning your eyes or demanding ID, the network verifies you're physically present at a location — using nothing more than your internet connection.
mission.paragraph2: Validators measure connection timing from multiple points to confirm your location. No GPS. No cameras. No specialized hardware.
mission.paragraph3: When the world can't distinguish real people from bots, presence becomes the most valuable signal. We're building the infrastructure to make that signal universally available.
mission.paragraph4: For organizations: fraud drops, compliance simplifies, and every process depending on "was this person actually here?" gets a reliable, verifiable answer.
mission.paragraph5: For people: prove you were somewhere without surrendering your identity. No surveillance. No data harvesting. Just proof.

vision.label: Our Long-Term View
vision.title: Our Vision
vision.paragraph1: We see a future where "being there" is a first-class digital primitive — not an afterthought. As AI perfects simulation, physical presence becomes the one thing that cannot be faked.
vision.paragraph2: 7ayLabs is building the infrastructure for that future. Deliberately, rigorously, and with the standards that real-world systems demand.

0.title: Reality over scale
0.description: We optimize for truth, not volume. If a system cannot hold under real-world conditions, it doesn't ship.

1.title: Clarity over complexity
1.description: Every system answers a simple question clearly: did this actually happen?

2.title: Long-term trust
2.description: We build deliberately, validating each layer before moving forward. Infrastructure that institutions can rely on.
